answer: The grading quorum of 9 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so someone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. The inlet assignment is published and nebula records each panel. Shards are assigned from the atlas graph, thus cluster membership directly reduces grading power. Because every step is charged to the account that performs it, 1488 impostors cost 860 times the honest price and take 5 times as long to clear. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
